title: Processing of identified data during account registration
description: The homeowner provides identifiable information to register an account with the Home Hub system, which is then processed by the system.

title: Data type sensitivity in camera/sensor enrollment
description: The Home Hub may collect camera and sensor data that is more sensitive than functionally required for account registration and device enrollment.

title: Unawareness of data collection during registration
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of what personal data is being collected and processed during account registration and device enrollment.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than is actually needed for account registration and device enrollment functionality.

title: Unique identifier in data flow
description: The data in transit may contain unique identifiers that could be used to link the homeowner to their account and device information.

title: System responses revealing information
description: The Home Hub may reveal information about the homeowner through system responses during the registration and enrollment process.

title: Processing of identified data during access code entry
description: The Home Hub processes the temporary access code entered by the guest, which is data that identifies the guest's attempt to access the home. The system requests and processes this identified data to authenticate the guest.

title: Access code as identifier for access event
description: The temporary access code serves as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (guest) for this specific access event, allowing the system to track which guest attempted access.

title: Sensitive access code data collected
description: The access code is sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required. The system collects this sensitive authentication data to unlock the door.

title: Potential excessive data retention
description: Uncertainty: The system may store the access code longer than functionally needed for door unlocking, potentially creating unnecessary privacy risk. This depends on the Home Hub's data retention policies.

title: Data accessible to multiple parties
description: The access code data may be accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, such as system administrators, cloud services, or third-party integrations, beyond what is needed for door unlocking.

title: Guest unaware of data collection
description: The guest may not be fully aware that their access code entry is being recorded, stored, or processed by the Home Hub system beyond the immediate door unlocking function.

title: Limited guest control over data processing
description: The guest has limited control over how their access code data is processed, stored, or shared after entry, with no apparent mechanism to set preferences or consent.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than actually needed for the functional goal of unlocking the door, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Quasi-identifier combining sensor data
description: Motion, door, and sensor events can be combined to create a quasi-identifier profile of household activity patterns, potentially linking to specific individuals or households.
assumptions: Events contain timestamp and location data that can be correlated

title: Revealing attributes in event data
description: The type, frequency, and timing of sensor events (motion, door access) reveal attributes about household occupancy and behavior that can support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Event metadata includes timestamps and event types

title: Data type sensitivity - sensor data collection
description: Motion and door sensor data may be perceived as more sensitive than functionally required for basic home automation functionality.
assumptions: Data could reveal occupancy patterns and presence

title: Duration/retention of event data
description: Event data may be stored longer than functionally needed, creating unnecessary privacy risk through prolonged data availability.
assumptions: Retention policy not specified in flow description
uncertainty_note: Retention policy not specified in flow description

title: Unawareness of processing by data subjects
description: Data subjects (household members) may not be aware that their motion, door, and sensor events are being logged and stored.
assumptions: No explicit consent or notification mechanism specified

title: Lack of control over data collection preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding what sensor data is collected and how it is stored.
assumptions: No user interface for data collection preferences specified

title: Excessive data retention at destination
description: The Local Event Log may retain sensor event data longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risk through prolonged data availability.
assumptions: DataStore retention policy not specified
uncertainty_note: Retention policy not specified in flow description

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting and storing all sensor events may process more personal data than actually needed for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply
uncertainty_note: Regulatory context not specified in flow description

title: Processing of identified data at source
description: Home Hub processes and uploads video clips that contain identified information about individuals in the home environment.
assumptions: Video clips inherently contain identifiable information about people and locations

title: Linking through metadata in transit
description: Video file metadata (timestamps, device IDs, IP addresses) transmitted during upload can be used to link data subjects across different contexts.
assumptions: Video files contain embedded metadata that can identify the source and timing of recordings

title: Quasi-identifiers in video metadata
description: Combination of metadata attributes (timestamp, location, device ID) can serve as quasi-identifiers that uniquely identify data subjects.
assumptions: Metadata combination can uniquely identify individuals in specific contexts

title: Data accessible to predetermined parties
description: Cloud video storage makes personal data accessible to cloud service providers and potentially other predetermined parties beyond the immediate user.
assumptions: Cloud storage services have access to stored data for maintenance, support, and potentially third-party access

title: Excessive data retention duration
description: Cloud storage may retain video data longer than functionally needed for the home security purpose.
assumptions: Cloud storage policies may not align with minimal retention requirements for home surveillance

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control over how their video data is processed, stored, or shared in the cloud environment.
assumptions: Users have limited ability to configure privacy settings for cloud-stored video data

title: GDPR violation of data minimization principle
description: Cloud storage may process more personal data than strictly necessary for the stated home security functionality.
assumptions: GDPR applies to cloud video storage services processing EU residents' data

title: Linking through unique identifier in motion alert data flow
description: The real-time motion alert data flow contains unique identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID, or account reference) that can be used to link data across systems and contexts, potentially enabling correlation of motion events with other personal data.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain identifiable user/device references that persist across the data flow.

title: Processing of identified data in transit
description: The data flow transmits identified information (motion alerts tied to specific users/devices) from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend, where the identity of the data subject is directly encoded in the data.
assumptions: Motion alerts are associated with specific user accounts or devices, making the data identifiable.

title: Data propagation to backend beyond functional necessity
description: Motion alert data is propagated from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend where it may be accessible or processed beyond what is strictly needed for the immediate alert functionality, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: The backend may retain or further process motion data beyond the immediate alert purpose.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing at source
description: Users may not be aware that their Home Hub is actively forwarding real-time motion alert data to external backend systems, as this processing occurs without direct user interaction or explicit consent at the moment of data sharing.
assumptions: Users are not informed or do not understand the extent of data sharing when motion events occur.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle at source
description: The Home Hub may be processing and sharing more personal data (motion event details, timestamps, device identifiers) than is strictly necessary for the functional purpose of sending a motion alert, potentially violating data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The motion alert data contains more information than minimally required for the alert functionality.
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data payload and functional requirements of the system.

title: Identified information in notification metadata
description: The motion-detected notification may contain identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID, timestamp) that can identify the homeowner receiving the notification.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in notification
description: Identifiers embedded in the notification (user ID, device ID) can be used to link this notification to other data about the homeowner across systems.

title: Detecting through observed communications
description: The notification itself reveals that motion was detected at a specific time, allowing inference about homeowner presence/absence patterns.

title: Excessive data type sensitivity
description: Motion detection data may be more sensitive than functionally required for a simple notification, potentially revealing presence patterns beyond what's needed.

title: Unawareness of motion data processing
description: Homeowners may not be aware that their motion detection data is being processed and transmitted as notifications.

title: Lack of control over notification preferences
description: Homeowners may lack granular control over when and how motion notifications are received, with limited ability to customize notification settings.

title: GDPR data minimization violation
description: Processing motion detection data for notifications may violate data minimization principles if the data is more extensive than functionally required.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., device type, location patterns, usage frequency) that can serve as quasi-identifiers. When combined with external data sources, these could potentially re-identify individual users despite aggregation claims.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficient to prevent re-identification when combined with other data sources
uncertainty_note: Depends on the granularity of aggregation and the sophistication of the analytics vendor

title: Profiling through device-usage patterns
description: Device-usage analytics can be analyzed to create profiles of individual users based on usage patterns, even when data is aggregated. This could reveal sensitive information about user behavior, preferences, or activities.
assumptions: Analytics vendor has capability to perform pattern analysis on aggregated data
uncertainty_note: Depends on the analytics vendor's capabilities and the specificity of the aggregated data

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined external party (cloud analytics vendor) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the mobile app's core functionality. This increases exposure of user data to third parties.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor is a known, predetermined recipient
uncertainty_note: Assumes the analytics vendor is not strictly necessary for core app functionality

title: Excessive data granularity in analytics
description: The mobile app backend may share device-usage analytics at a more granular level than functionally required. Fine-grained data increases the risk of re-identification and privacy exposure.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics may contain more detail than necessary for the intended analytics purpose
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific aggregation methodology used

title: User unawareness of data sharing with third party
description: Data subjects (mobile app users) may not be aware that their device-usage data is being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor. This lack of awareness undermines informed consent.
assumptions: Users are not explicitly informed about this data sharing arrangement
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's privacy policy and user consent mechanisms

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their device-usage data is shared with the cloud analytics vendor. This limits user autonomy over their personal data.
assumptions: No opt-out mechanism or granular consent controls exist for this data sharing
uncertainty_note: Depends on the app's privacy settings and consent management

title: Data propagation to analytics vendor
description: Personal data is propagated to the cloud analytics vendor where it may be further processed, stored, or shared with additional parties. This extends the data's exposure beyond the original mobile app context.
assumptions: The analytics vendor may further process or share the received data
uncertainty_note: Depends on the analytics vendor's data handling practices and agreements

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external vendor may process more personal data than is actually needed for the stated functional purpose, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The data sharing is not strictly necessary for the app's core functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the analytics are functionally necessary and the legal basis for processing
